questions.question_english: In the context of Biotechnology, what term is used for a biological medicine that is highly similar to another already approved biological medicine (reference medicine)?
questions.explanation_english: A biosimilar is a biological medical product that is highly similar in structure, efficacy, safety, and quality to an already approved original reference biological medicine. Unlike standard synthetic chemical generic drugs, biological therapies are manufactured using complex living biological systems. Consequently, biosimilars require rigorous analytical, non-clinical, and clinical comparability studies to demonstrate that minor structural differences do not affect therapeutic safety or clinical performance in human patients.
